name: agent-farm
description: Mission control for your local Claude Code agents: live fleet status, cost analytics, session explorer, health & optimization insights.

No agents found yet.
[Add Agent Root Folder](command:agentfarm.addAgentRoot)
Agent Farm scans the configured root folders for agent directories (folders containing a CLAUDE.md).
[Open Guide](command:agentfarm.openGuide)

[Set Up a Working Example](command:agentfarm.setupExample)

[Add Task](command:agentfarm.addTask)

[Open Guide](command:agentfarm.openGuide)

Give a goal to a lead agent and a team — the lead plans round by round, delegates, and finishes with an honest verdict.

walkthroughs.title: Agent Farm: Setup in Five Steps
walkthroughs.description: From live monitoring to your first autonomous job — mission control for your agent fleet.

steps.title: 1 · Introduce your agents
steps.description:
Agent Farm treats every folder with a CLAUDE.md under your root folders as an agent.
[Add Agent Root](command:agentfarm.addAgentRoot)

steps.title: 2 · Install the live hooks
steps.description:
Hooks forward every agent event (prompt, tool, permission wait) to the local listener — the timeline and notifications run on them.
[Install Live Hooks](command:agentfarm.installHooks)

steps.title: 3 · Open the Dashboard
steps.description:
Costs, health and the Farm Status card — which subsystem is dormant, at a glance.
[Open Dashboard](command:agentfarm.openDashboard)

steps.title: 4 · Set up your first automation
steps.description:
A working example in one click: an inbox duty, a morning briefing or a two-agent chain.
[Set Up Example Automation](command:agentfarm.setupExample)

steps.title: 5 · Explore the guide
steps.description:
The built-in guide (English by default, Türkçe selectable; 25 scenarios): media pipeline, webhook bridge, multi-agent chains…
[Open Guide](command:agentfarm.openGuide)

view/title.when: view == agentfarm.agents || view == agentfarm.sessions || view == agentfarm.insights || view == agentfarm.feed || view == agentfarm.toolbox

agentFarm.guideLanguage.description: Language for the in-app help surfaces (Guide, Quick Start, Examples). English by default; choose Türkçe for Turkish. You can also switch from the language toggle inside the guide panel. More languages can be added over time.

agentFarm.agentRoots.description: Root folders scanned for agent directories. Subfolders containing CLAUDE.md, .claude or memory/ become agents. A root whose subfolders are agents is a nest — its own CLAUDE.md counts as shared instructions, not an agent; a root with no agent-like subfolders is one agent itself. Manage this comfortably in the Agent folders section of Farm Settings.

agentFarm.excludeAgentDirs.description: Folders that are never treated as agents, even when they look like one. Compared case- and slash-insensitively. Easiest managed via Exclude/Include in the Agent folders section of Farm Settings.

agentFarm.newAgentModel.description: Default model written into a new agent's .claude/settings.local.json when the agent is created via Agent Farm — an alias (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable) or a full model id. Empty = write no model, the Claude CLI default applies. Existing agents' models are managed per agent in the Agent folders section of Farm Settings.

agentFarm.modelAliases.description: Your model name knowledge base: the names/ids offered in every model picker (the per-agent model dropdown in Agent folders, the mission model suggestions, the Start Session… launcher). Add a new model name here ONCE and it appears in every picker permanently — model names change over time, this list is yours to keep current. Every picker also accepts a custom free-text entry for anything not listed.

agentFarm.web.enabled.markdownDescription: Serve a **read-only web view** of the farm — the same figures the panel shows, sized for a phone: what needs you, what is running, per-agent and per-project cost, recent sessions. Off by default. While VS Code is open the extension serves it; when VS Code is closed the **headless service** takes the port over and keeps serving the last snapshot (and says so on the page). Bound to `127.0.0.1` unless `agentFarm.web.bind` says otherwise, and **a token is always required** — there is no route that starts, stops or changes anything. Use **Open Web View…** to get the URL.

agentFarm.web.port.description: Port for the read-only web view (the live-hook listener uses agentFarm.livePort, 8377, and must stay separate).

agentFarm.web.bind.markdownDescription: `local` — only this machine (127.0.0.1). `lan` — reachable from your phone or a second machine on the same network. LAN exposure is opt-in on purpose; the token stays mandatory either way, and the view stays read-only.

agentFarm.web.token.description: Access token for the web view. Generated for you the first time you enable it; anyone with this token can READ the farm's dashboard, so treat it like a password. Empty = the server refuses to start.

agentFarm.telegram.enabled.markdownDescription: Let a **Telegram chat talk to your agents**: send a message, the agent the chat is bound to runs it headlessly, and the answer comes back in the same thread. Off by default; the bot token lives in the Agent Farm **secret vault** (never in settings) — set it up with **Connect Telegram…**. Two rails are always on: a message from a chat that is not in `agentFarm.telegram.allowedChats` is refused (it is told its own chat id, so allowing it is one copy), and chat-started runs stop at `agentFarm.telegram.maxDailyUSD` per day. Commands in chat: `/agent <name>` · `/agents` · `/status` · `/cancel` · `/help`.

agentFarm.telegram.allowedChats.description: Telegram chat ids allowed to drive the farm. EMPTY = nobody can (the bridge answers every message with a refusal and its own chat id). This is the access list for something that spends money — keep it to your own chats.

agentFarm.telegram.maxDailyUSD.description: Ceiling on what chat-started runs may cost per day (API-equivalent). 0 = no runs from chat at all; commands like /status keep working.

agentFarm.telegram.defaultAgent.description: Agent a new chat talks to before it picks one with /agent. Empty = a chat must bind an agent first.

model.description: --model for every session (alias or full id). Empty = the agent's own setting / the CLI default.

effort.description: --effort for every session. Empty = no flag.

permissionMode.description: --permission-mode for every session. Empty = no flag (asks, as configured).

agentFarm.launchDefaults.markdownDescription: How **every** interactive session starts — Start, Continue and Resume alike, from the tree, the palette or a keybinding. Set once instead of typing `--model` into a terminal all day. Every field is optional and an empty one emits no flag at all, so the default `{}` starts exactly the bare `claude` it always did. The **Start Session…** launcher (`ctrl+alt+s`) shows these as inherited values and can override them for one launch, or write itself back here.

name.description: profile name shown in the launcher

prompt.description: optional first prompt sent with the session

agentFarm.launchProfiles.markdownDescription: Saved launch setups offered by the **Start Session…** launcher — "deep review" (opus + xhigh + plan), "quick fix" (sonnet + acceptEdits), and so on. The launcher's *Save this as a profile…* row writes here; nothing is applied until you pick one.

agentFarm.notifyConsoleTurnEnd.markdownDescription: Tell you when a **Console** turn finishes and you are not watching that conversation — a notice carrying what the turn took, with a button that opens it. Never fires for the session on your screen, and never for a turn you interrupted. The Console's own signals (the card's *your turn* state and the count on its tab) do not depend on this.

agentFarm.speakerLabelTemplate.markdownDescription:
How the AI participant is labelled in conversations (Turns page, Session Viewer, and their Markdown exports) — where it used to say `ASSISTANT`/`claude`. The label is **derived from each message's model id**, so a Gemini or Codex turn labels itself correctly. Compose it from these tokens; anything else is literal text, so a template with no tokens is a fixed label of your own:

- `{ai}` — engine: `claude` · `gemini` · `codex`
- `{model}` — model family: `opus` · `sonnet` · `haiku` · `gpt` · …
- `{version}` — version: `4.8` · `3.5` · …
- `{raw}` — raw model id (`opus-4-8`, vendor prefix stripped)

Examples: `{ai}` → CLAUDE · `{model} {version}` → OPUS 4.8 · `{ai} {model} ({version})` → Claude Opus (4.8) · `MyBot` → a fixed label. Empty = `{ai}`. Case is set by `speakerLabelCase`; `speakerLabelFallback` covers unknown models.

enumDescriptions: Match the page — Session Viewer upper (like USER), Turns lower (like user/tool). The current default.
As-is — leave the template's own case untouched (use for a fixed brand label)
agentFarm.speakerLabelCase.description: Case applied to the AI speaker label (see agentFarm.speakerLabelTemplate).

agentFarm.speakerLabelFallback.description: AI speaker label shown when the model id yields nothing to fill the template (unknown engine, <synthetic>, or missing). Never 'assistant' — this is an agent.

agentFarm.claudeDir.description: Path to the Claude Code data directory. Leave empty to use ~/.claude.

name.description: Machine label shown on sessions (e.g. laptop)

dir.description: Path to that machine's synced .claude folder

agentFarm.extraClaudeDirs.description: Additional (read-only, synced) Claude data folders from other machines — e.g. a Syncthing/OneDrive copy of the laptop's ~/.claude. Their sessions appear with a ⇄ machine badge.

agentFarm.activeThresholdSeconds.description: A session is considered ACTIVE if its transcript changed within this many seconds.

agentFarm.staleMemoryDays.description: Memory files untouched for more than this many days are flagged as stale.

agentFarm.contextBudgetTokens.description: Warn when an agent's fixed context load (CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md + AGENTS.md) exceeds this estimated token budget.

agentFarm.forecastDays.description: How many days ahead the Task Forecast projects scheduled runs.

agentFarm.windowTokenLimit.description: Optional token limit for the rolling 5-hour usage window (subscription plans). 0 hides the progress bar and shows raw totals.

enumDescriptions: Weigh the kinds of token AND the model: one Sonnet input token = 1, Opus = 5, Haiku = 1/3. The default — a haiku test must not read as expensive as opus work.
Weigh only the KINDS of token (output x5, 1h cache-write x2, 5m cache-write x1.25, cache-read x0.1) and ignore which model ran.
Turn the weighting off: the ⚖ figure becomes the raw total.
agentFarm.quotaWeightMode.description: How the ⚖ figure (what work costs the plan's rolling limit, as opposed to how many tokens moved) is derived. Calibrated against the real endpoint on 2026-08-04 by sampling utilization twice inside one window: 29% → 82% over 28 minutes and 96 API calls cost 38.13M raw / 24.86M weighted-model-aware / 4.97M weighted-model-flat, i.e. a full 5-hour limit of about 72M raw, 47M model-aware or 9.4M model-flat FOR THAT WORKLOAD. Almost all of it ran on Opus, so that sample cannot tell model-aware and model-flat apart — sample a day with real haiku or sonnet work to separate them.

agentFarm.quotaWeights.description: Override the ⚖ weight table. Empty = use the built-in one. Each entry: { match (regex on the model id), input, output, cacheWrite (5-minute TTL), cacheWrite1h (1-hour TTL), cacheRead } — all relative to ONE SONNET INPUT TOKEN = 1. Built in: opus and fable { input 5, output 25, cacheWrite 6.25, cacheWrite1h 10, cacheRead 0.5 }, sonnet { 1, 5, 1.25, 2, 0.1 }, haiku { 0.333, 1.667, 0.417, 0.667, 0.033 }. ‼️ CACHE WRITES ARE PRICED BY TTL AND THE 1-HOUR RATE IS THE ONE THAT APPLIES HERE: measured on this machine, 17 923 938 of 17 923 938 cache-creation tokens were 1-hour and none were 5-minute. A usage block that reports no split is charged at the 1-hour rate. Deliberately separate from agentFarm.pricing: correcting a billing rate must not silently move the limit gauge. First matching rule wins; an unmatched model falls back to the sonnet row, never to zero.

match.description: Regex matched against the model id (case-insensitive).

input.description: Weight of one fresh input token.

output.description: Weight of one output token — thinking is billed here too, and it is the biggest spender in a turn.

cacheWrite1h.description: Weight of one 1-hour-TTL cache-creation token — the rate that actually applies on this machine.

cacheRead.description: Weight of one cache-read token. This is 94-99% of any raw total, which is why the raw figure says so little about the limit.

enumDescriptions: Brake on whichever ceiling is further along — the safe default when both are configured.
Brake only on the ⚖ weighted figure against windowWeightedTokenLimit.
Brake only on the raw total against windowTokenLimit — how it behaved before the weighted figure existed.
agentFarm.quotaBrakeBasis.description: Which figure the quota guard (quotaGuardPercent) and the model-downgrade rule (quotaDowngradePercent) read when deciding how full the 5-hour window is. A ceiling that is not configured is simply not consulted, whatever this says — set windowTokenLimit and/or windowWeightedTokenLimit first.

agentFarm.windowWeightedTokenLimit.description: Optional limit for the rolling 5-hour window measured in WEIGHTED tokens (⚖) instead of raw ones. A cache-read token is a tenth of a fresh input token and an output token is five, while 94-99% of a raw total is cache reads — so the raw total of a full window ranges 111M-175M across days that hit the very same wall, and the weighted total of those same windows sits at 18-21M. Set this to what your plan actually allows (watch the ⚖ figure in the status bar for a window where you hit the limit) and the quota guard and the model-downgrade rule brake on it. 0 = off; the raw windowTokenLimit keeps working exactly as before, and setting both brakes on whichever is further along.

agentFarm.planUsageRefreshMinutes.description: How often your Claude subscription limits are re-read from Anthropic while the fleet is IDLE, in minutes — nothing is running, so they can only change by the clock. While an agent is actually mid-turn the faster planUsageActiveRefreshSeconds beat takes over. One beat is shared by the status-bar indicator, the Dashboard's "Plan usage" card and the usage.plan bridge op — they never make separate requests. 0 turns the automatic refresh off in BOTH windows; the card's ⟳ and the indicator's "Check now" still work. Only the OAuth session Claude Code stores locally is read; it is never written to.

agentFarm.planUsageActiveRefreshSeconds.description: How often the same figures are re-read while at least one agent is mid-turn, in seconds — that is when they are actually moving, and when you are watching them. A session that is open but waiting for your next prompt is idle and uses the minutes setting above. The switch is instant in both directions: a turn starting and a turn ending each trigger one immediate read. Minimum 30 seconds, and that floor is enforced in code: the endpoint is undocumented and answers a too-frequent poller with a persistent HTTP 429, so a fast setting is not a preference it will honour. A 429 is met with an automatic backoff (3 → 6 → 12 → 15 min) that one success clears; the ⟳ button asks anyway. Ignored when planUsageRefreshMinutes is 0 (automatic refresh off).

agentFarm.planUsageStatusBar.description: Keep your plan's session countdown and usage percentages in the VS Code status bar — "3h 49m - 86% / wk 41%": time left in the current session window, how much of it is gone, and how much of the week. Visible while you work without opening anything. Hover for every limit with its reset time and the beat it is running on, click for the Dashboard card. Hidden automatically on a machine with no Claude subscription login (API key / Bedrock / Vertex).

agentFarm.planUsageWarnPercent.description: The status-bar usage indicator turns yellow once any of your plan's limits reaches this percentage.

agentFarm.planUsageDangerPercent.description: …and red at this one. Set it to 101 to never go red.

agentFarm.maxTranscriptMessages.description: Maximum number of messages rendered in the session viewer.

agentFarm.contextWindowTokens.description: Context-window ceiling for the session viewer's 'Context now' gauge. 0 = auto-detect from the session's model (unknown models show the raw token count without a percent); set a value to force a fixed ceiling.

agentFarm.liveMonitor.description: Run the local live-event listener (127.0.0.1) that receives Claude Code hook events.

agentFarm.livePort.description: Port for the local live-event listener. Re-run 'Install Live Hooks' after changing it.

agentFarm.stuckThresholdSeconds.description: A working session with no hook events for this long is marked STALLED.

agentFarm.notifyPermission.description: Show a notification when an agent is waiting for a permission approval.

agentFarm.notifyStuck.description: Show a notification when an agent looks stalled.

agentFarm.notifyTurnEnd.description: Show a notification every time an agent finishes its turn.

agentFarm.taskExtraArgs.description: Extra CLI arguments appended to every task's claude command, e.g. "--model haiku" to run routine automation on a cheaper model.

agentFarm.externalTerminal.description: Open claude session terminals (Start/Continue/Resume) in the OS terminal — Windows Terminal when available — instead of the integrated terminal. Avoids xterm.js rendering glitches (ghost spaces, lost lines) in long TUI sessions. Farm tasks stay in the integrated terminal so their status can be tracked. Toggle via 'Terminal Rendering Fix…'.

agentFarm.judgeArgs.description: CLI arguments for internal verification (judge) calls — keep this on a cheap model.

agentFarm.maxConcurrentTasks.description: Maximum tasks running at once across the whole farm (0 = unlimited). Excess starts are deferred and launched automatically.

agentFarm.maxConcurrentPerAgent.description: Maximum tasks running at once per agent (0 = unlimited).

agentFarm.quotaGuardPercent.description: Defer automatic task starts when the 5h window reaches this percent of windowTokenLimit (0 = off; requires windowTokenLimit).

agentFarm.outputsMaxMB.description: Size cap for the archived task outputs folder; oldest unreferenced outputs are pruned (0 = unlimited).

agentFarm.mediaAuthSecret.description: Name of the vault secret holding your fal.ai key (store it via 'Agent Farm: Set Secret…').

agentFarm.replicateAuthSecret.description: Name of the vault secret holding your Replicate API token (store it via 'Agent Farm: Set Secret…'). Used for media models with a 'replicate:' prefix.

agentFarm.replicateBaseUrl.description: Override the Replicate API base URL (testing / self-hosted proxy). Empty = https://api.replicate.com.

agentFarm.codexHome.description: Codex CLI home whose sessions/ rollout transcripts feed the external-session history. Empty = ~/.codex.

agentFarm.geminiDir.description: Gemini CLI tmp dir whose chat files feed the external-session history. Empty = ~/.gemini/tmp.

agentFarm.mediaBaseUrl.description: Override the fal.ai queue base URL (testing / self-hosted proxy). Empty = https://queue.fal.run.

agentFarm.reportDir.description: Default folder where agents' full 'notices.post report' files are written (naming YYYY-MM-DD_<name>.md). Empty = D:\zone\know\note\obsidian\00_AGENT_AREA\00_OUTPUT\10_REPORT.

agentFarm.answerDir.description: Folder where a work item's detailed answer (not a user-requested report) is written by queue.stamp (naming YYYY-MM-DD_<agent>_<name>.md). Empty = D:\zone\know\note\obsidian\00_AGENT_AREA\00_OUTPUT\01_CEVAPLAR.

agentFarm.queue.targets.description: Optional routing-target suggestions (repos/areas) offered in the work queue's add form and filter, in addition to the discovered agent names. Empty by default — free text, nothing hardcoded.

agentFarm.queue.groupSize.description: Work queue batching: a group of same-target items FIRES for delegation once it reaches this many items (mechanical threshold; the manager also fires on age/urgency).

agentFarm.queue.maxAgeHours.description: Work queue batching: the oldest item in a group forces the group to fire after this many hours, so nothing starves (anti-starvation cap).

label.description: source label shown in the gallery (default: folder name)

projectId.description: auto-assign ingested assets to this production id

sceneId.description: auto-assign to this scene id (needs projectId)

agentFarm.ingestFolders.description: Media ingest folders (downloads, render exports…): scanned every 30s; new image/video/audio files are registered into the Media Gallery in place (no copy). Files older than 48h at scan time are ignored.

agentFarm.mediaBudgetMonthUSD.description: Warn once per month when estimated media cost over the last 30 days exceeds this amount (USD). 0 = off.

agentFarm.mediaPricing.description: Estimated media pricing rules (USD): {match, usd, per: request|image|second}. Verify against fal.ai pricing.

agentFarm.notifyWebhookUrl.description: Forward farm notifications (permission, stalled, budget, workflow done/failed) to this webhook URL as JSON — e.g. an n8n webhook that relays to Telegram. Supports {secret:NAME}.

agentFarm.notifyWebhookEvents.description: Which notification types are forwarded to notifyWebhookUrl.

agentFarm.dailyDigest.description: Send a compact daily fleet scorecard to notifyWebhookUrl after this local time (HH:MM, e.g. "21:30"); "off" disables. No model call — plain data. Manual: 'Send Daily Digest Now'.

match.description: case-insensitive regex tested against the incoming text

agent.description: agent name that takes the work

agentFarm.dispatchRules.description: Dispatcher routing rules for 'dispatch' triggers — first matching regex wins. Example: [{"match": "uyku|kaygı", "agent": "psikolog"}].

agentFarm.dispatchClassifier.description: When no dispatch rule matches, let the cheap model (judgeArgs) pick the agent from CLAUDE.md role hints.

agentFarm.embeddingsProvider.description: Semantic search embeddings: 'gemini' (Google API, GEMINI_API_KEY secret) or 'openai' (any OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint — incl. fully local Ollama/LM Studio via embeddingsBaseUrl, no key needed).

agentFarm.embeddingsModel.description: Embedding model id. Empty = provider default (gemini-embedding-001 / text-embedding-3-small; for Ollama e.g. nomic-embed-text).

agentFarm.embeddingsBaseUrl.description: Override the embeddings endpoint base URL. For local Ollama: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1

agentFarm.embeddingsSecret.description: Vault secret name holding the embeddings API key. Empty = GEMINI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY by provider; local endpoints may need none.

agentFarm.semanticMaxSessions.description: How many most-recent sessions the semantic index covers.

agentFarm.browserAllowHosts.description: Global host allowlist for browser steps (subdomains included). A browser step refuses to run if neither this nor its own allowHosts covers the URL.

agentFarm.browserApproval.description: 'ask' = confirm every browser step before it runs (recommended); 'auto' = run allowlisted browser steps without asking.

name.description: profile name shown in the task wizard

headless.description: command template with {prompt} and {args}, e.g. gemini -p "{prompt}"

interactive.description: optional interactive template; falls back to headless

agentFarm.cliProfiles.description: Alternative CLI executors for tasks (gemini / codex / …). Non-claude tasks get output archiving and exit-code status; deep monitoring (transcripts, live hooks, cost) stays Claude-specific.

file.description: path to the synced relay-*.jsonl written by farmRelay.js on that machine

agentFarm.relayFeeds.description: Live relay feeds from other machines (J2): run farmRelay.js there ('Save Relay Script for Another Machine…'), sync its output file here, list it in this setting.

agentFarm.packGalleryRepos.description: Agent pack gallery sources: git URLs (shallow-cloned into extension storage) or local folders containing .agentpack files.

agentFarm.digestTtsModel.description: fal.ai TTS model id for the spoken daily briefing (e.g. an ElevenLabs TTS endpoint on fal — verify the exact id on fal.ai). Empty disables 'Speak Daily Briefing'.

agentFarm.digestTtsFolder.description: Folder the spoken briefing mp3 is saved into (e.g. a phone-synced folder). Empty = autoReportFolder.

source.description: which launches the rule applies to

agent.description: case-insensitive regex on the agent name (empty = any)

promptMatch.description: case-insensitive regex on the prompt (empty = any)

agentFarm.modelPolicy.description: Rule-based model routing for farm-launched tasks; first match wins. Example: [{"source": "trigger", "model": "haiku"}] runs all trigger-born work on a cheap model.

agentFarm.quotaDowngradePercent.description: When the 5h window reaches this percent of windowTokenLimit, farm-launched tasks are forced onto quotaDowngradeModel (0 = off).

agentFarm.quotaDowngradeModel.description: Model forced when the quota downgrade kicks in.

agentFarm.permissionLint.description: Audit each agent's permission rules (blanket allows, dangerous patterns, unused broad rules) and surface findings in Insights.

agentFarm.pulse.description: Synthetic pulse checks: a fixed cheap prompt per agent + cheap judge verifies the answer matches the agent's identity (uses judgeArgs; small API cost per agent). Manual: 'Run Pulse Check Now'.

agentFarm.insightAutoDelegate.markdownDescription: Insight categories that are **automatically delegated** to the insight's own agent as a headless task when they appear (warnings/errors only; 24h cooldown per problem; only the task-runner window queues them). Empty = off. Example: `["memory-index", "duties", "guardrail"]`. Categories are shown next to each row in the Insights view. This spends agent time — enable deliberately.

agentFarm.qualitySample.description: Automatically sample recent session outputs and score them 1-5 with the cheap-model judge (uses judgeArgs; small API cost per sample). Manual: 'Sample Output Quality Now'.

agentFarm.qualitySamplesPerAgent.description: How many not-yet-scored recent sessions per agent each quality sampling run scores.

agentFarm.suggestScan.description: Weekly cheap-model scan of your follow-up messages for repeated corrections, proposing CLAUDE.md rules (Insights view). Manual: 'Scan for Instruction Suggestions…'.

agentFarm.weeklySummary.description: Once per ISO week, write a three-sentence human-language fleet summary (cheap model) as a notification — and into autoReportFolder if set.

agentFarm.queueAutoAdvance.description: When a task finishes (its terminal closes), automatically start the next queued task for that agent.

agentFarm.autoReport.description: Automatically write a fleet report into autoReportFolder (checked hourly while VS Code is open).

agentFarm.autoReportFolder.description: Folder for automatic fleet reports (e.g. a folder inside your Obsidian vault).

agentFarm.autoReportDays.description: Period (in days) covered by automatic fleet reports.

agentFarm.trendAlertFactor.description: Warn when an agent's 7-day cost reaches this multiple of the previous 7 days. 0 disables trend alerts.

agentFarm.costAnomalyMinUsd.description: Statistical cost-anomaly detector (median + MAD over 14 days): ignore days below this USD level. 0 disables the detector.

agentFarm.agentRowCostUnit.description: Unit for the daily-usage suffix shown on each agent's row in the Agents view. Tokens by default since cost reads $0 until an agentFarm.pricing rule matches the model.

agentFarm.evalRunArgs.description: CLI arguments for eval-set replay calls. Keep a cheap model for routine regression checks; empty = the agent's default model (more faithful, more expensive).

agentFarm.autoReportIncludeOutputs.description: Append the archived task-outputs digest to automatic fleet reports.

agentFarm.budgets.description: Daily USD budgets by agent name (API-equivalent value). Use "*" for a fleet-wide budget. Example: {"psikolog": 20, "*": 50}. Warns at 80%, alerts when exceeded.

agentFarm.includeUnmatchedProjects.description: Also include Claude Code sessions whose working directory is outside the configured agent roots (shown under 'Other projects').

agentFarm.pricing.description: Model pricing rules in USD per million tokens. First regex match wins.

agentFarm.livingChecks.description: Living page checks. Each entry is {label, when:{kind,path,except,minCount,hours,recursive}, level:info|warn|alert, hint?}. The precondition is read as "TRUE = needs attention" - e.g. kind:fileMissing on today's diary file, or kind:folderHasFiles on an inbox that should be empty. Paths support {today} / {yesterday}.

agentFarm.projectsRoot.description: Folder that holds your project folders. A new project is offered a folder inside it, and Rescan Project Folders walks it. Leave empty to choose a folder by hand for every project.

agentFarm.projectSkeleton.description: What a new project folder is built out of. Empty = the shipped default (Charter / Plan / Backlog / Backloglog / People / Worklog, plus 10_Notes, 20_Decisions, 30_Deliverables, 40_Resources, 90_Archive, 90_Archive/_tracks, _AF). Set your own to follow a vault naming convention: a path ending in / is a folder; {project} {id} {status} {date} {yymmdd} expand; "role" is what Agent Farm looks a document up by — never its file name, so you can rename anything afterwards; and "holds" is how a FOLDER is found for the same reason (decisions are one file each, and the backlog track ledger is not a note).

path.description: path inside the project folder; a trailing / means a folder

role.description: what this document IS — how Agent Farm finds it, whatever it is called

holds.description: what this FOLDER is for, when it cannot be found by a role: decisions (one file each) or tracks (the backlog track ledger)

template.description: initial content; the placeholders above expand

agentFarm.projectStaleDays.description: Days of silence after which a project still marked active is flagged as quiet. 0 turns the check off. A project list without this becomes a graveyard nobody dares tidy.

agentFarm.projectContextExtra.description: One line of your own added to the project context every session gets (see the ◧ chip above the Console composer). This is where an installation points its agents at its own rules — e.g. "Your constitution's _REF/project-session.md applies to this session." Empty by default: Agent Farm ships general, and what an agent should DO with a project is yours to say.

agentFarm.noticeStaleHours.description: Hours after which an UNREAD level-3+ notice counts as ignored: it escalates on the Living page and in the status bar. A board nobody reads is the same as one nobody wrote to.

agentFarm.idleSessionNoticeMinutes.description: Minutes a session may sit waiting for your input before ONE notice is posted about it (0 disables). An idle session never blocks the farm, so it is not a Needs You row — but one left waiting all afternoon is a loop that quietly never closed.

agentFarm.consoleDropZone.description: Whether the Console page listens for a file dropped anywhere on it. Turn this off if drag-and-drop misbehaves on your machine; 📎 (Attach) and pasting a screenshot are unaffected either way.

agentFarm.promptSnippetsFile.description: The markdown file holding the phrases you say to an agent over and over. Farm Settings → Saved prompts is where you pick it, see what was read out of it, and open it. Right-click any button that SENDS text in the Console — Send · Send into turn · Send after turn · Start session — and those blocks are offered to paste into the message box. Only text inside ``` fences is offered; everything around them is your own notes. Left empty, Agent Farm falls back to a built-in path in the vault while that file exists — so this stays empty on a machine where it does not, and nothing has to be cleared.
